title: Causative: have / get something done
summary: Use 'have/get + object + past participle' when you arrange for someone else to do something for you.

theory.markdown:
The **causative** structure is used when you **arrange** for someone else to do something for you — you pay for or request the service.

**have + object + past participle**: (more common, neutral)
*I had my hair cut.* (a hairdresser cut it)
*She has her nails done every week.*

**get + object + past participle**: (slightly more informal, also common)
*He got his car repaired.* (a mechanic repaired it)

**Compare:**
- *I cut my hair.* (I did it myself)
- *I had my hair cut.* (someone cut it for me)

**All tenses work with have/get:**
*I'm having my house painted.* (currently arranged)
*She had her computer fixed.* (past)
*We will have the roof replaced.* (future)

theory.title: Causative forms
rows: They will have the room decorated.
He has had his bike repaired.
He has got his bike fixed.
I didn't have my hair cut.
Did you have your eyes tested?

items.source: We're having the kitchen renovated next month.
items.translation: W przyszłym miesiącu remontujemy kuchnię (zlecamy remont).

items.source: She needs to get her eyes tested.
I had my wallet stolen on the tube.
items.translation: Ukradli mi portfel w metrze. (to also uses this structure for unplanned events)

exercises.prompt: I ___ my teeth ___ (check) at the dentist last week. (had)
She ___ her portrait painted by a famous artist.
exercises.explanation: Both 'had' and 'got' are correct in the causative.

answers: Have you had your photos taken?
Have you got your photos taken?

exercises.sentence: She had cut her hair by a hairdresser.
answers: She had her hair cut by a hairdresser.
exercises.explanation: Causative structure: have + OBJECT first, then past participle.

exercises.prompt: They ___ their house ___ (paint) this summer. (will / get)
